'''Thomas Jerome Schaefer''' is an American mathematician.

He obtained his Ph.D. in December 1978 from the [[University of California, Berkeley]], where he worked in the Department of Mathematics. His Ph.D. advisor was [[Richard M. Karp]].<ref>{{mathGenealogy|31947}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://math.berkeley.edu/people/grad/thomas-jerome-schaefer|title=Thomas Jerome Schaefer &#124; Department of Mathematics at University of California Berkeley}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | author=Thomas J. Schaefer | title=On the Complexity of Some Two-Person Perfect-Information Games | journal=Journal of Computer and System Sciences | volume=16 | number=2 | pages=185–225 | year=1978 | mr= 490917 |doi=10.1016/0022-0000(78)90045-4| doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite book | author=Thomas J. Schaefer | contribution=Complexity of Decision Problems Based on Finite Two-Person Perfect-Information Games | title=Eighth Annual [[ACM Symposium on Theory of Computing]] | publisher=ACM | pages=41–49 | year=1976 |mr= 0451853}}</ref> 

He is well-known for his [[Schaefer's dichotomy theorem|dichotomy theorem]], stating that any problem generalizing [[Boolean satisfiability problem|Boolean satisfiability]] in a certain way is either in the [[P (complexity class)|complexity class P]] or is [[NP-complete]].<ref>{{cite book | contribution-url=http://www.ccs.neu.edu/home/lieber/courses/csg260/f06/materials/papers/max-sat/p216-schaefer.pdf | author=Schaefer, Thomas J. | contribution=The complexity of satisfiability problems | title=Proc. 10th Ann. ACM Symp. on Theory of Computing | pages=216–226 | year=1978 |mr= 521057}}</ref>
